openers.prompt_en: At a science fair, Asha writes down three questions about a solar cooker, then waits after the demonstration to ask the teacher. Is she curious or bored? Give one clue.
openers.prompt_hi: Science fair mein Asha solar cooker par teen sawaal likhti hai aur demonstration ke baad teacher se poochhne ke liye rukti hai. Woh curious hai ya bored? Ek clue batao.
openers.answer: Curious; she writes questions and waits to ask them.
acceptable: Curious; she stayed to ask the teacher.
Curious, because she wants to know more.
hints: What does Asha do after watching?
Her actions show whether she wants to learn more.
She seems ___ because she writes questions.
She is curious: she records questions and stays to ask them.

verified.solverAnswer: Curious. She thinks of questions in advance and waits to ask.

openers.prompt_en: Rohan wants to join the school cricket team. He practises before class but hides his kit when the coach walks past. Does he seem confident or nervous about speaking to the coach? Give one clue.
openers.prompt_hi: Rohan school cricket team join karna chahta hai. Woh class se pehle practice karta hai, par coach ko aate dekh kit chhupa leta hai. Coach se baat karne ko lekar woh confident hai ya nervous? Ek clue batao.
openers.answer: Nervous; he hides his kit when the coach passes.
acceptable: Nervous, because he avoids showing the coach his kit.
hints: What changes when the coach comes near?
Notice what Rohan tries to keep out of sight.
He seems ___ because he hides his kit.
He seems nervous: he hides his kit from the coach.

verified.solverAnswer: Nervous. He hides his kit to avoid the coach.

harder.prompt_en: Nila asks why the school garden dries out. Her classmates investigate and discover a leaking pipe. What message does this short story suggest: questions can lead to solutions, or problems disappear if ignored?
harder.prompt_hi: Nila poochhti hai ki school garden kyun sookh raha hai. Classmates jaanch karte hain aur leaking pipe dhoondhte hain. Is chhoti kahani ka message kya hai: sawaal solutions tak le ja sakte hain, ya ignore karne se problems khud khatam hoti hain?
acceptable: Asking questions can lead to solutions.
hints: What started the investigation?
Connect Nila’s first action to the discovery.
The story suggests that asking ___ can help solve problems.
Questions can lead to solutions: Nila’s question prompted an investigation.

harder.prompt_en: A metro announcement says, ‘The last train leaves at 10 p.m.’ Ask for the departure time using ‘When’. Say the complete question.
harder.prompt_hi: Metro announcement mein hai: ‘The last train leaves at 10 p.m.’ Departure time poochhne ke liye ‘When’ se shuru hone wala poora English question bolo.
harder.answer: When does the last train leave?
acceptable: When does the last train leave
hints: What time detail are you asking about?
With a singular subject, use a helper before the subject.
When ___ the last train leave?
When does the last train leave? ‘Does’ comes before the subject.

verified.solverAnswer: When does the last train leave?

harder.prompt_en: The students were eager to see their science project tested. Complete the sentence with the correct form of ‘eager’: ‘They watched ___ as the results appeared.’
harder.prompt_hi: Students apna science project test hote dekhne ke liye eager the. ‘Eager’ ka sahi form laga kar sentence poora karo: ‘They watched ___ as the results appeared.’
hints: Which word tells us how they watched?
Change the describing word into a word describing the action.
They watched ___ as the results appeared.
Eagerly: it describes how they watched.

harder.prompt_en: Read: ‘Sana’s family said the riverbank was no place to study. She carried her notebook there anyway and asked the water-quality team how they tested pollution.’ Which feeling best explains Sana’s actions: curiosity, boredom, or anger?
harder.prompt_hi: Padho: ‘Sana ke gharwalon ne kaha ki nadi kinare padhai nahin hoti. Phir bhi woh notebook lekar gayi aur water-quality team se poochha ki pollution kaise test karte hain.’ Sana ke kaam ko kaunsi feeling samjhati hai: curiosity, boredom, ya anger?
hints: What does Sana do despite her family’s view?
Look at what she asks the team.
Her questions suggest she wants to ___.
Curiosity: she goes there to learn how testing works.

harder.prompt_en: A notice says, ‘The river-cleaning volunteers meet at the school gate every Sunday.’ Ask where they meet. Begin with ‘Where’ and write the complete question.
harder.prompt_hi: Notice mein likha hai: ‘The river-cleaning volunteers meet at the school gate every Sunday.’ Woh kahaan milte hain, yeh poochho. ‘Where’ se shuru karke poora English question likho.
harder.answer: Where do the river-cleaning volunteers meet?
hints: Which part of the notice gives the place?
Use a helper verb before the subject.
Where ___ the river-cleaning volunteers meet?
Where do the river-cleaning volunteers meet? ‘Do’ comes before the subject.

verified.solverAnswer: Where do the river-cleaning volunteers meet?

harder.prompt_en: At the river survey, Kavya was eager to examine the water samples. Complete the report using the correct form of ‘eager’: ‘Kavya examined the samples ___.’
harder.prompt_hi: River survey mein Kavya water samples check karne ke liye eager thi. ‘Eager’ ka sahi form lagakar report poori karo: ‘Kavya examined the samples ___.’
hints: Which word tells us how Kavya examined them?
Change the adjective into an adverb.
Kavya examined the samples ___ (eager + ending).
Eagerly: the adverb describes how Kavya examined the samples.

ongrade.prompt_en: Read: ‘Tara kept her questions about the river in a notebook. When the librarian offered her a book on rivers, she borrowed it immediately, though she had never visited the library before.’ What does Tara’s decision suggest about her feelings?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Padho: ‘Tara nadi ke baare mein apne sawaal notebook mein likhti thi. Librarian ne nadiyon par kitab di, toh woh pehli baar library jaakar use turant le aayi.’ Tara ke faisle se uski feelings ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
ongrade.answer: She was eager to learn more about rivers.
acceptable: She wanted to learn more about rivers
She was eager to find answers
hints: What had Tara been recording before visiting the library?
Notice how quickly she accepted a chance to read.
Her decision shows she wanted to ___ about rivers.
She was eager to learn: she borrowed the book immediately.

verified.solverAnswer: She is curious and eager to learn about rivers.

ongrade.prompt_en: Read: ‘Farah asked why their school tap ran dry each afternoon. She spoke to the caretaker, checked the water tank with a teacher, and discovered a leak. The school repaired it.’ What message about asking questions does this story suggest?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Padho: ‘Farah ne poochha ki school ka nal har dopahar sukha kyun rehta hai. Usne caretaker se baat ki, teacher ke saath tank check kiya aur leak dhoondh liya. School ne use theek karaya.’ Sawaal poochhne ke baare mein kahani kya sandesh deti hai?
ongrade.answer: Asking questions can lead to investigation and solutions.
acceptable: Questions help us investigate and solve problems
Asking why can help us find answers and fix problems
hints: What happened after Farah asked her question?
Connect her question, investigation and the repair.
Asking questions can lead to ___ and solutions.
Questions can lead to investigation and solutions; Farah found the leak.

verified.solverAnswer: Asking questions can lead to solving problems.

ongrade.prompt_en: The river changes course after heavy rain. Ask a question beginning with ‘Why’ about this change. Use ‘does’ and keep the verb in its base form.
ongrade.prompt_hi: Sentence hai: ‘The river changes course after heavy rain.’ Is badlav ke baare mein ‘Why’ se sawaal banao. ‘Does’ lagao aur verb ka base form use karo.
ongrade.answer: Why does the river change course after heavy rain?
acceptable: Why does the river change its course after heavy rain?
hints: Where will the helping verb go in your question?
Place ‘does’ before the subject; remove the verb’s ending.
Why ___ the river change course after heavy rain?
Why does the river change course after heavy rain? ‘Does’ takes the verb’s ending.

verified.solverAnswer: Why does the river change course after heavy rain?

openers.prompt_en: Read aloud: “My first code failed to run. / I fixed a line and tried again. / Try again, try again!” On the repeated last line, which words should receive extra stress: “try again” or “first code”?
openers.prompt_hi: Ye lines zor se padho: “My first code failed to run. / I fixed a line and tried again. / Try again, try again!” Repeated last line mein kis par zyada zor doge: “try again” ya “first code”?
hints: Which words does the speaker say more than once?
Give the repeated message a clear beat.
Stress the words “___” on the last line.
Stress “try again”; it is the repeated message.

openers.prompt_en: A poem says: “The first clay pot cracked. / Meera shaped another. / Keep shaping, keep shaping!” Does the repeated line suggest learning through practice or getting everything right immediately?
openers.prompt_hi: Ek poem mein hai: “The first clay pot cracked. / Meera shaped another. / Keep shaping, keep shaping!” Repeated line kya batati hai: practice se seekhna ya turant sab sahi karna?
hints: What does Meera do after the pot cracks?
Connect her next action to the repeated line.
The line encourages ___ despite a mistake.
Learning through practice; Meera makes another pot.

harder.prompt_en: “The team lost its first kabaddi match. / They trained before the next. / Step back in, step back in! / They lost once more, then trained again. / Step back in, step back in!” Why repeat the last line?
harder.prompt_hi: Kabaddi team par ye lines padho: “The team lost its first kabaddi match. / They trained before the next. / Step back in, step back in! / They lost once more, then trained again. / Step back in, step back in!” Last line baar-baar kyun aati hai?
harder.answer: To emphasise that the team keeps trying despite losing.
acceptable: To show they do not give up.
Haar ke baad bhi koshish jaari rakhne par zor dene ke liye
hints: What happens after each loss?
Notice how the repeated instruction follows a setback.
The repetition stresses that the team keeps ___ despite losing.
It emphasises perseverance: they keep trying after losses.

verified.solverAnswer: To emphasize perseverance after each setback.

harder.prompt_en: Read the line endings in this stanza: “The runners trained beneath the light / Their footsteps beat upon the ground / They came back stronger the next night / Their cheers became the loudest sound.” Is the rhyme scheme AABB or ABAB?
harder.prompt_hi: Is stanza ke line endings dekho: “The runners trained beneath the light / Their footsteps beat upon the ground / They came back stronger the next night / Their cheers became the loudest sound.” Rhyme scheme AABB hai ya ABAB?
hints: Which line endings sound alike?
Give matching end sounds the same letter.
The first and third lines match; write the pattern as ___.
ABAB; alternate lines rhyme.

harder.prompt_en: Complete this plan for the school science fair: “If our model ___ (work) after the repair, we ___ (show) it tomorrow.” Give both missing verb forms in order.
harder.prompt_hi: School science fair ke plan mein blanks bharo: “If our model ___ (work) after the repair, we ___ (show) it tomorrow.” Dono verb forms order mein batao.
hints: Which clause states the condition?
Use present tense for the condition and will for its result.
If our model ___, we will ___ it.
Works, will show; the if-clause uses present tense.

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'On the metro, Aarav put away his phone and noticed the station announcements, the cool air and the voices around him. His journey felt richer.' Which is the main idea: 'Aarav rode the metro' or 'Paying attention to our senses enriches ordinary moments'?
openers.prompt_hi: Passage padho. Main idea kya hai: 'Aarav metro mein gaya' ya 'Apni senses par dhyaan dene se roz ke pal aur achchhe lagte hain'?
openers.answer: Paying attention to our senses enriches ordinary moments
acceptable: Apni senses par dhyaan dene se roz ke pal aur achchhe lagte hain
Noticing our senses makes ordinary moments richer
hints: Which option covers the whole experience?
A main idea is broader than one event.
The details about sounds and air support the idea that ____.
Paying attention to our senses enriches ordinary moments; the details show this change.

verified.solverAnswer: Paying attention to our senses enriches ordinary moments

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'Before tasting her grandmother's dal, Meera noticed its aroma. She realised she usually ate in a hurry without noticing either.' Why does the writer include Meera's realisation: to explain a recipe or to encourage readers to notice their senses?
openers.prompt_hi: Passage padho. Meera ko jo ehsaas hua, writer ne woh kyun bataya: recipe samjhane ke liye ya readers ko apni senses par dhyaan dene ke liye?
openers.answer: To encourage readers to notice their senses
acceptable: To make readers value their senses
Readers ko apni senses par dhyaan dene ke liye
hints: What might readers do differently afterward?
Think about the writer's message, not the food.
Meera's change invites readers to ____.
To encourage readers to notice their senses; Meera had overlooked an everyday experience.

verified.solverAnswer: to encourage readers to notice their senses

harder.prompt_en: Read: 'After a power cut, Zoya followed her father's voice to the door. When the lights returned, she noticed how easily she had ignored his voice before.' Why mention both the power cut and the returning lights? Answer in a short phrase.
harder.prompt_hi: Passage padho. Writer ne power cut aur lights waapas aane, dono ka zikr kyun kiya? Ek chhote phrase mein batao.
harder.answer: To show that losing a sense briefly can make us value it more
acceptable: To make readers value the senses they normally take for granted
Kisi sense ki kami mehsoos karke uski ahmiyat samajhna
hints: What changed in Zoya's attention?
Compare what she noticed during and after the power cut.
The contrast helps readers value ____.
To show that losing a sense briefly can make us value it more.

verified.solverAnswer: to show contrast between ignoring and noticing sound

harder.prompt_en: Choose the correct sentence for an imagined situation: 'If I lost my glasses, I would ask for help' or 'If I lose my glasses, I would asked for help'?
harder.prompt_hi: Imagined situation ke liye sahi sentence chuno: 'If I lost my glasses, I would ask for help' ya 'If I lose my glasses, I would asked for help'?
harder.answer: If I lost my glasses, I would ask for help
acceptable: If I lost my glasses I would ask for help
hints: Is this a real plan or an imagined situation?
An imagined condition uses a past-form verb; would takes a base verb.
If I ___ my glasses, I would ___ for help.
If I lost my glasses, I would ask for help; both verbs fit the pattern.

verified.solverAnswer: If I lost my glasses, I would ask for help

harder.prompt_en: At a school concert, Kavya paid careful attention to the tabla throughout the performance. Which fits best: 'heard the tabla', 'listened to the tabla' or 'looked at the tabla'?
harder.prompt_hi: School concert mein Kavya ne poori performance tabla ki awaaz par dhyaan diya. Kaunsa phrase best hai: 'heard the tabla', 'listened to the tabla' ya 'looked at the tabla'?
hints: Was Kavya paying attention deliberately?
Choose the verb for actively focusing on a sound.
Kavya ___ the tabla throughout the performance.
Listened to the tabla; it shows deliberate attention to its sound.

ongrade.prompt_en: Read: 'During a cricket match, Rohan heard the crowd cheer and felt the cool breeze, but kept checking his phone. Later, he realised how much he had missed.' Which is the main idea: A) The crowd was loud or B) We often overlook what our senses let us experience?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Passage padho: Cricket match mein Rohan ne crowd ki cheering suni aur thandi hawa mehsoos ki, par phone dekhta raha. Baad mein use laga ki usne bahut kuch miss kiya. Main idea kya hai: A) Crowd loud tha ya B) Hum aksar senses se milne wale experiences ko nazarandaaz kar dete hain?
ongrade.answer: B) We often overlook what our senses let us experience
acceptable: We often overlook what our senses let us experience
We take our senses for granted
hints: Which option covers the whole passage?
Separate the match detail from the broader reflection.
The writer moves from Rohan's experience to the idea that we ___.
B is correct: the match details support a broader reflection about our senses.

verified.solverAnswer: B) We often overlook what our senses let us experience.

ongrade.prompt_en: Complete this imagined situation with the correct verb forms: 'If our school library ___ (stay) open after classes, I ___ (read) there every evening.'
ongrade.prompt_hi: Is imagined situation mein verbs ke sahi forms bharo: 'If our school library ___ (stay) open after classes, I ___ (read) there every evening.'
acceptable: If our school library stayed open after classes, I would read there every evening
hints: Is this a fact or an imagined situation?
Use the second conditional pattern for both blanks.
If the library ___ open, I ___ there.
Stayed; would read: an imagined condition takes past form, then would plus base verb.

verified.solverAnswer: If our school library stayed open after classes, I would read there every evening.

ongrade.prompt_en: At the science exhibition, Nisha stood silently for several minutes, observing a model of the night sky. Choose the most precise verb: Did she see, watch, or gaze at the model?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Science exhibition mein Nisha kai minute chupchaap khadi hokar night sky ka model dekhti rahi. Sabse precise verb chuno: Kya usne model ko see, watch, ya gaze at kiya?
hints: Was her glance brief or prolonged?
Choose the verb that suggests steady, intent looking.
Nisha stood silently for minutes; she ___ the model.
Gaze at: it describes looking steadily for a long time.

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'A rescue worker found a trapped myna. It kept calling whenever she walked away, so she searched nearby and found its chick caught in a net.' Why did the myna keep calling?
openers.prompt_hi: Padho: 'Ek rescue worker ko phansi hui myna mili. Jab bhi woh door jaati, myna awaaz karti. Paas dhoondhne par uska bachcha jaal mein phansa mila.' Myna baar-baar awaaz kyun kar rahi thi?
openers.answer: To draw attention to its trapped chick
acceptable: To get the worker to find its chick
hints: What changed after the worker searched nearby?
Connect the repeated calls with what she found.
The myna wanted the worker to notice ___.
Its chick was trapped; the calls drew the worker's attention.

verified.solverAnswer: It was calling for its chick

openers.prompt_en: During a coastal cleanup in Kochi, volunteers spotted many fish swimming together. Complete the report: 'A ___ of fish swam past the pier.'
openers.prompt_hi: Kochi mein coastal cleanup ke dauran volunteers ne kai machhliyon ko saath tairte dekha. Report poori karo: 'A ___ of fish swam past the pier.'
hints: Which collective noun describes fish swimming together?
Choose the group word used specifically with fish.
A ___ of fish swam past the pier.
School: a school of fish is the usual collective noun.

verified.solverAnswer: A school of fish swam past the pier.

harder.prompt_en: Read: 'At the shelter, a dog refused food but kept scratching at a locked shed. The caretaker opened it and found three puppies inside. The dog then ate.' Why did the dog refuse food at first?
harder.prompt_hi: Padho: 'Shelter mein ek kutte ne khana nahi khaya, par band shed ko khurachta raha. Caretaker ne shed khola toh andar teen puppies mile. Phir kutte ne khana kha liya.' Usne pehle khana kyun nahi khaya?
harder.answer: It wanted the caretaker to rescue the puppies
acceptable: It was worried about the trapped puppies
It wanted the puppies let out
To draw attention to the puppies
hints: What did the caretaker discover after following the dog's signal?
Its behaviour changed only after the shed was opened.
It refused food because it wanted help for ___.
It wanted the puppies rescued; it ate once they were found.

verified.solverAnswer: It wanted to lead the caretaker to the puppies

harder.prompt_en: A vet reported, 'The calf is safe.' Choose the correct sentence: A) The vet told that the calf was safe. B) The vet said that the calf was safe. C) The vet said the farmer that the calf was safe.
harder.prompt_hi: Vet ne kaha, 'The calf is safe.' Sahi reported sentence chuno: A) The vet told that the calf was safe. B) The vet said that the calf was safe. C) The vet said the farmer that the calf was safe.
acceptable: The vet said that the calf was safe
hints: Is a listener named immediately after the reporting verb?
Check which verb works before 'that' without naming a listener.
The vet ___ that the calf was safe.
B is correct: 'said that' needs no listener after 'said'.

verified.solverAnswer: B) The vet said that the calf was safe.

harder.prompt_en: At a wildlife rescue centre, an owl makes its usual call while a dog moves its tail from side to side. Which pair describes these actions: A) hoots and wags B) neighs and roars C) chirps and moos?
harder.prompt_hi: Wildlife rescue centre mein ullu apni aam awaaz nikalta hai aur kutta poonch idhar-udhar hilata hai. Kaunsi jodi sahi hai: A) hoots and wags B) neighs and roars C) chirps and moos?
hints: Which word names an owl's call?
For the dog, choose a word describing tail movement.
An owl ___; a dog ___ its tail.
A: an owl hoots, and a dog wags its tail.

ongrade.prompt_en: Read: 'At a Jaipur animal shelter, a parrot repeatedly called out when the vet approached a quiet dog. The vet noticed the dog was guarding an injured puppy hidden beneath a bench.' Why might the parrot have called out?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Jaipur ke animal shelter mein vet ek chup baithe dog ke paas gayi toh parrot baar-baar awaaz karne laga. Vet ne dekha ki bench ke neeche injured puppy hai aur dog uski raksha kar raha hai. Parrot ne awaaz kyun ki hogi?
ongrade.answer: To draw the vet’s attention to the injured puppy
acceptable: To alert the vet about the injured puppy
To get the vet to notice the injured puppy
Vet ka dhyaan injured puppy ki taraf dilane ke liye
hints: What did the vet discover after hearing the calls?
Connect the calls to the animal needing help.
The parrot wanted the vet to notice the ___.
The injured puppy: the calls drew the vet’s attention to it.

verified.solverAnswer: To alert the vet about the hidden injured puppy.

ongrade.prompt_en: A wildlife volunteer writes, 'We saw a ___ of wolves crossing the road near the forest.' Which collective noun completes the report: flock, herd, pack, or school?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Wildlife volunteer ki report hai: 'We saw a ___ of wolves crossing the road near the forest.' Kaunsa collective noun sahi hai: flock, herd, pack, ya school?
hints: Which option names a group of wolves?
Collective nouns depend on the kind of animal.
We saw a ___ of wolves.
Pack: a group of wolves is called a pack.

ongrade.prompt_en: A vet said to Meera, 'The owl is ready to fly.' Which report is correct: A) The vet said Meera that the owl was ready to fly. B) The vet told Meera that the owl was ready to fly?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Vet ne Meera se kaha, 'The owl is ready to fly.' Kaunsi reported sentence sahi hai: A) The vet said Meera that the owl was ready to fly. B) The vet told Meera that the owl was ready to fly?
acceptable: The vet told Meera that the owl was ready to fly
hints: Which reporting verb can take a person directly after it?
Check how Meera follows the reporting verb.
The vet ___ Meera that the owl was ready to fly.
B: ‘told’ can take Meera directly as its object.

verified.solverAnswer: B) The vet told Meera that the owl was ready to fly.

openers.prompt_en: At a school concert, a singer says, ‘I put the stage in my pocket and walked home.’ What makes this line nonsense humour: an impossible action or an ordinary action?
openers.prompt_hi: School concert mein singer kehta hai, ‘Maine poora stage jeb mein rakha aur ghar chala gaya.’ Is line mein nonsense humour kis wajah se hai: impossible action ya ordinary action?
hints: Could someone really do what the singer claims?
Think about the size of the object and the action.
Putting that object in a pocket is an ___ action.
An impossible action: a stage cannot fit in a pocket.

openers.prompt_en: Read these line endings from a poem about a metro ride: train / rain / light / night. Is their rhyme scheme AABB or ABAB?
openers.prompt_hi: Metro ride wali poem ki lines ke ending words hain: train / rain / light / night. Inka rhyme scheme AABB hai ya ABAB?
hints: Which ending sounds match?
Give matching sounds the same letter, in line order.
The first two endings match; write their letters as ___ ___.
AABB: the first pair rhymes, then the second pair rhymes.

harder.prompt_en: A poem about a cricket match ends its four lines with: ball / cheer / wall / near. Write its rhyme scheme using A and B.
harder.prompt_hi: Cricket match wali poem ki chaar lines ke ending words hain: ball / cheer / wall / near. A aur B se rhyme scheme likho.
hints: Does the second ending rhyme with the first or fourth?
Mark the first sound A; give a different sound B.
The third ending matches the ___ ending.
ABAB: alternate lines have matching ending sounds.

harder.prompt_en: Two lines describe a delayed train: ‘It arrived ten minutes late’ and ‘It arrived a thousand years late.’ Which uses exaggeration for humour, and why? Answer in a short phrase.
harder.prompt_hi: Late train ke liye do lines hain: ‘It arrived ten minutes late’ aur ‘It arrived a thousand years late.’ Humour ke liye exaggeration kis line mein hai, aur kyun? Chhote phrase mein batao.
harder.answer: ‘A thousand years late’—it makes the delay impossibly long
acceptable: a thousand years late because the delay is impossibly long
the second line; it greatly exaggerates the delay
hints: Which delay sounds beyond anything a timetable could show?
Exaggeration makes a real problem much bigger than reality.
The ___ line stretches the delay beyond belief.
‘A thousand years late’: it makes the delay impossibly long.

verified.solverAnswer: The second line, because it heavily exaggerates the delay.
verified.note: Both note exaggeration in second line

harder.prompt_en: At a school event, Mira is a good speaker. Complete the sentence with the correct adverb: ‘Mira spoke ___, even when the microphone stopped working.’
harder.prompt_hi: School event mein Mira ek good speaker hai. Sahi adverb se sentence poora karo: ‘Mira spoke ___, even when the microphone stopped working.’
hints: Does the blank describe Mira or how she spoke?
Use an adverb for an action, not an adjective for a person.
The adverb form needed after ‘spoke’ is ___.
Well: it describes how Mira spoke.

harder.prompt_en: A poem about a delayed train has four line endings: train / light / night / rain. Write its rhyme scheme using letters.
harder.prompt_hi: Delayed train wali kavita ki chaar lines ke aakhri shabd hain: train / light / night / rain. Letters se iska rhyme scheme likho.
hints: Which line endings sound alike?
Give matching sounds the same letter.
The first and last lines share a letter: _ _ _ _.
ABBA: train rhymes with rain; light rhymes with night.

harder.prompt_en: At the school concert, a poet says, ‘The singer’s whisper shook the whole city.’ Is the humour mainly from exaggeration or from a word having two meanings?
harder.prompt_hi: School concert par poet kehta hai, ‘The singer’s whisper shook the whole city.’ Humour zyada kis se aata hai: exaggeration se ya ek word ke do meanings se?
hints: Could a whisper really have that effect?
Notice how far the poet stretches its impact.
This huge claim is an example of ___.
Exaggeration: a whisper cannot shake a whole city.

harder.prompt_en: Choose the correct words in order: ‘The announcer gave a ___ (good/well) introduction, but spoke too ___ (quick/quickly) for the audience to follow.’
harder.prompt_hi: Sahi words order mein chuno: ‘The announcer gave a ___ (good/well) introduction, but spoke too ___ (quick/quickly) for the audience to follow.’
hints: What does each blank describe?
Use an adjective for a noun and an adverb for an action.
An ___ introduction; spoke too ___.
Good, quickly: ‘good’ describes introduction; ‘quickly’ describes spoke.

ongrade.prompt_en: At a cricket match, a poet writes: ‘The scoreboard cheered when I got out; the crowd displayed the runs.’ Which image makes this nonsense humour rather than an ordinary match report?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Cricket match par poet likhta hai: ‘The scoreboard cheered when I got out; the crowd displayed the runs.’ Kaunsi image ise ordinary match report ke bajay nonsense humour banati hai?
hints: Which object acts like a person?
Look for an impossible action, not an unusual score.
The impossible action is ___.
The scoreboard cheered; a scoreboard cannot cheer.

verified.solverAnswer: The scoreboard and crowd are given human, impossible actions.
verified.note: Solver explains but mismatches key image

ongrade.prompt_en: A four-line poem ends with these words, in order: gate, sky, late, fly. What is its rhyme scheme: ABAB or AABB?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Chaar-line ki poem ke end words order mein hain: gate, sky, late, fly. Iska rhyme scheme ABAB hai ya AABB?
hints: Which line endings sound alike?
Give matching sounds the same letter.
The pattern is ___ .
ABAB: gate rhymes with late; sky rhymes with fly.

ongrade.prompt_en: Choose the correct word in each blank: ‘Riya gave a good performance at the school event; she performed ___. After forgetting one line, she continued ___.’ Options: well or good; confident or confidently.
ongrade.prompt_hi: School event mein Riya ne good performance di; she performed ___. Ek line bhoolne ke baad, she continued ___. Har blank ke liye sahi word chuno: well ya good; confident ya confidently.
hints: What do the blanks describe: Riya or her actions?
Words describing how actions happen are adverbs.
She performed ___ and continued ___.
Well; confidently. Both describe how she acted.

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'HOST: Our chief guest will speak after the dance. ARUN: Then why is she standing beside the microphone now? HOST: She is checking its height!' What misunderstanding makes Arun's question funny?
openers.prompt_hi: Dialogue padho: chief guest dance ke baad bolengi, lekin ab microphone ke paas khadi hain. Arun ko kya galatfahmi hui?
openers.answer: He thinks the chief guest is about to speak before the dance.
acceptable: She is going to speak before the dance
Arun thinks the speech is starting early
hints: What does Arun expect to happen at the microphone?
Compare the announced programme with what Arun assumes.
Arun thinks the speech will happen ___ the dance.
He thinks she will speak before the dance; she is only adjusting the microphone.

verified.solverAnswer: Arun thinks 'speak' means talking right then, but the host means 'speak' later as a scheduled speaker.
verified.note: solver explains but misses exact misunderstanding

openers.prompt_en: At the school library, you need a book from the librarian's desk. Complete the polite request: '___ you please pass me that book?' Choose: Could or Must.
openers.prompt_hi: School library mein librarian se book leni hai. Polite request poori karo: '___ you please pass me that book?' Could ya Must?
hints: Are you making a request or giving an order?
Choose the modal that makes a request sound courteous.
‘___ you please pass me that book?’
Could; it asks for help politely rather than giving an order.

harder.prompt_en: Read: 'NISHA: Tell the judge our team is ready. DEV: Our team is ready—except our robot has lost its head! NISHA: I meant the team leader, not the robot's head!' What misunderstanding changes the conversation?
harder.prompt_hi: Dialogue padho: Nisha judge ko team ke ready hone ki baat kehna chahti hai, par Dev robot ke head ki baat karta hai. Galatfahmi kya hai?
harder.answer: Dev thinks Nisha means the robot, while she means the team leader.
acceptable: Dev mistakes the robot for the team leader
He thinks she is talking about the robot instead of the team leader
hints: Which two people or things are being confused?
Notice what Dev mentions and what Nisha corrects.
Dev talks about ___, but Nisha means ___.
Dev thinks she means the robot; Nisha means the team leader.

verified.solverAnswer: Nisha uses 'head' to mean the team leader, but Dev understands it as the robot's physical part.

harder.prompt_en: Before a school debate, Meera says, 'We need to break the ice with the visiting team.' Kabir brings a hammer to the water cooler. Why is his action funny?
harder.prompt_hi: Debate se pehle Meera kehti hai, 'We need to break the ice with the visiting team.' Kabir water cooler par hammer le aata hai. Uska kaam funny kyun hai?
harder.answer: He takes 'break the ice' literally instead of understanding it means to help people feel comfortable.
acceptable: He thinks it means breaking real ice, not starting a friendly conversation
hints: Is Meera talking about frozen water?
Think about what helps two teams talk comfortably.
Kabir acts on the ___ meaning, not the intended meaning.
He takes the idiom literally; Meera means to ease the awkwardness.

verified.solverAnswer: He takes 'break the ice' literally instead of its idiomatic meaning.

harder.prompt_en: In a play: 'RIYA: (quietly, glancing at the sleeping guest) The music has started.' You are playing Riya. Should you say the bracketed words aloud or speak the line softly while looking towards the guest?
harder.prompt_hi: Play mein likha hai: 'RIYA: (quietly, glancing at the sleeping guest) The music has started.' Riya ka role karte waqt brackets ke words bologe, ya line dheere bolkar guest ki taraf dekhoge?
harder.answer: Speak the line softly while looking towards the guest.
acceptable: Speak softly and glance at the guest
Line dheere bolkar guest ki taraf dekho
hints: What do brackets tell an actor to do?
Stage directions guide performance; they are not dialogue.
Say the spoken line ___ and glance towards the guest.
Speak softly and glance at the guest; the brackets give acting directions.

verified.solverAnswer: Speak the line softly while looking towards the guest.

openers.prompt_en: Meera tested a rain alarm. She connected the wires, placed a drop of water on the sensor, heard the buzzer, and wrote down the result. Complete her retelling: 'First, I connected the wires. Then, I placed a drop on the sensor. After that, ___. Finally, I wrote down the result.'
openers.prompt_hi: Meera ne rain alarm test kiya: wires jode, sensor par paani ki boond rakhi, buzzer suna, aur result likha. Retelling poori karo: 'First, I connected the wires. Then, I placed a drop on the sensor. After that, ___. Finally, I wrote down the result.'
hints: Which event comes between placing the drop and writing the result?
Follow the order of events, not the order of importance.
After that, I ___; finally, I wrote down the result.
I heard the buzzer; that happened before she recorded the result.

openers.prompt_en: Arjun's phone stand tipped over during a school exhibition. He said, 'The base needs to be wider,' and began a new sketch. Was his attitude discouraged or determined?
openers.prompt_hi: School exhibition mein Arjun ka phone stand gir gaya. Usne kaha, 'Base aur wide honi chahiye,' aur naya sketch banane laga. Uska attitude discouraged tha ya determined?
hints: What did Arjun do after the stand tipped over?
Notice whether he stopped or looked for an improvement.
His new sketch shows he was ___ rather than giving up.
Determined; he used the problem to plan a better stand.

harder.prompt_en: A school's solar charger project went like this: Nisha drew a circuit, the team bought parts, they assembled it, a wire came loose during testing, and they repaired it. Which happened immediately before the repair: assembling the charger or discovering the loose wire?
harder.prompt_hi: School ke solar charger project mein Nisha ne circuit banaya, team ne parts kharide, charger assemble kiya, testing mein wire loose mila, phir repair kiya. Repair se turant pehle kya hua: charger assemble karna ya loose wire ka pata chalna?
acceptable: the wire came loose during testing
hints: Trace the events from the start of the project.
Look at what testing revealed before the team made a change.
Testing revealed ___; after that, they repaired it.
Discovering the loose wire; the repair followed that finding.

harder.prompt_en: Complete both verbs: 'I ___ (check) the prototype when the power ___ (go) out.' Use past continuous for the ongoing action and simple past for the interruption.
harder.prompt_hi: Dono verbs bharo: 'I ___ (check) the prototype when the power ___ (go) out.' Jo kaam chal raha tha uske liye past continuous, aur beech mein hui ghatna ke liye simple past use karo.
acceptable: I was checking the prototype when the power went out
hints: Which action was already in progress?
Give the ongoing action two verb parts; use one for the interruption.
I ___ checking the prototype when the power ___ out.
Was checking; went. The checking was ongoing when the power failed.

harder.prompt_en: A science-club notice says, 'Riya will demonstrate her new device.' Rewrite it as 'Riya's ___ will be at the science club,' using a noun formed from 'demonstrate'.
harder.prompt_hi: Science-club notice mein likha hai, 'Riya will demonstrate her new device.' 'Demonstrate' se noun bana kar sentence poora karo: 'Riya's ___ will be at the science club.'
hints: Does the blank need an action verb or a noun?
Name the event rather than saying what Riya will do.
Change 'demonstrate' into a noun: Riya's ___ will be at the club.
Demonstration; it names the event where Riya shows her device.

verified.solverAnswer: Riya's demonstration will be at the science club

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'Meera sends a paper kite into the sky with a note: Perhaps someone beyond these rooftops will see my hello.' Which idea is central: winning a kite contest or hoping to connect with someone far away?
openers.prompt_hi: Padho: 'Meera patang par note bhejti hai: Shayad chhaton ke paar koi mera hello dekhe.' Central idea kya hai: patang competition jeetna ya door kisi se judne ki umeed?
openers.answer: Hoping to connect with someone far away
acceptable: door kisi se judne ki umeed
hints: What does Meera want the note to do?
Look beyond the kite to her purpose.
The central idea is her hope to ____.
Hoping to connect with someone far away; she wants her hello seen.

verified.solverAnswer: hoping to connect with someone far away

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'The monsoon clouds marched over the school ground.' Which technique gives clouds a human action: metaphor or personification?
openers.prompt_hi: Padho: 'The monsoon clouds marched over the school ground.' Clouds ko insaan jaisa action dene wali technique kaunsi hai: metaphor ya personification?
hints: Can clouds literally march?
Notice whose action the verb usually describes.
Giving a non-human thing a human action is ____.
Personification; marching is a human action given to clouds.

harder.prompt_en: Read: 'My message is a seed sailing across the lake.' Why does calling the message a seed suit a poem about hope? Answer in a short phrase.
harder.prompt_hi: Padho: 'My message is a seed sailing across the lake.' Umeed wali kavita mein message ko seed kehna kyun theek hai? Chhote phrase mein batao.
harder.answer: It may grow into a new connection
acceptable: it could grow into a friendship
isse nayi dosti shuru ho sakti hai
hints: What can happen to a seed later?
Think about what a message might begin.
The message could lead to a new ____.
It may grow into a new connection, just as a seed grows.

verified.solverAnswer: It can grow into something beautiful and far-reaching.

harder.prompt_en: Complete both verbs: 'Every Sunday, Arjun ___ (write) a note, and his cousins ___ (send) it with a paper boat.'
harder.prompt_hi: Dono verbs bharo: 'Every Sunday, Arjun ___ (write) a note, and his cousins ___ (send) it with a paper boat.'
hints: Who does each action?
Check whether each subject is singular or plural.
Arjun ___; his cousins ___.
Writes; send. Singular Arjun takes -s; plural cousins do not.

harder.prompt_en: At a school book exchange, you leave a note for whoever takes your book. Choose the sentence that expresses a hope: 'I hope you enjoy this story' or 'I enjoyed this story.'
harder.prompt_hi: School book exchange mein tum apni book lene wale ke liye note chhodte ho. Umeed batane wala sentence chuno: 'I hope you enjoy this story' ya 'I enjoyed this story.'
harder.answer: I hope you enjoy this story
acceptable: I hope you enjoy this story.
hints: Which sentence looks towards the reader's experience?
One sentence describes your past; the other expresses a wish.
Choose the sentence about what you want the reader to ____.
I hope you enjoy this story; it expresses a wish for the reader.

verified.solverAnswer: I hope you enjoy this story

harder.prompt_en: Read: 'Aarav folds his exam timetable into a paper boat and lets it travel down the rainwater drain. Tomorrow is still uncertain, but he smiles as it sails away.' Does the boat mainly suggest escape from exams or hope despite uncertainty?
harder.prompt_hi: Yeh padho: 'Aarav apna exam timetable modkar kagaz ki naav banata hai aur use baarish ke paani mein baha deta hai. Kal kya hoga, pata nahi, phir bhi woh muskurata hai.' Naav kya dikhati hai: exams se bachna ya anishchitata ke bawajood umeed?
acceptable: hope even though the future is uncertain
hints: What does Aarav’s smile suggest?
Look at how he feels about tomorrow, not just the timetable.
His smile suggests ___ despite not knowing tomorrow’s result.
Hope despite uncertainty: he smiles although tomorrow is unknown.

harder.prompt_en: Complete both verbs in the simple present: 'Neither of the two boats ___ (carry) a name, but both ___ (carry) a message.'
harder.prompt_hi: Simple present mein dono verbs bharo: 'Neither of the two boats ___ (carry) a name, but both ___ (carry) a message.'
hints: Which word controls each verb: 'neither' or 'boats'?
Treat 'neither' as singular and 'both' as plural.
Neither ___ a name, but both ___ a message.
Carries; carry. 'Neither' takes a singular verb; 'both' takes a plural verb.

harder.prompt_en: You are writing to a student who may find your paper boat next week. Which message expresses a possible future hope: 'I hope you find this boat' or 'I wish you had found this boat'?
harder.prompt_hi: Agle hafte tumhari kagaz ki naav kisi student ko mil sakti hai. Future ki mumkin umeed kaun-sa message batata hai: 'I hope you find this boat' ya 'I wish you had found this boat'?
harder.answer: I hope you find this boat
acceptable: I hope you find this boat.
hints: Has the student found the boat yet?
Choose the expression for something that may still happen.
For a possible future event, use 'I ___ you find this boat.'
I hope you find this boat. Finding it is still possible.

verified.solverAnswer: I hope you find this boat

ongrade.prompt_en: Read: 'Riya launches a paper boat after the rain. She knows it may sink before reaching anyone, yet she writes, “I hope someone finds this.”' Is the central idea hope despite uncertainty or certainty of success?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Padho: 'Riya baarish ke baad kagaz ki naav chhodti hai. Use pata hai naav kisi tak pahunchne se pehle doob sakti hai, phir bhi woh likhti hai, “I hope someone finds this.”' Central idea kya hai: anishchitata ke bawajood umeed, ya safalta ka yakeen?
acceptable: hope even though the boat may sink
hints: Does Riya know what will happen to the boat?
Notice the difference between what she knows and what she hopes.
She is uncertain, but she still expresses ___.
Hope despite uncertainty: she sends the boat although it may sink.

ongrade.prompt_en: Read: 'On the flooded street, paper boats drifted beneath the streetlights like tiny golden lamps.' Does 'tiny golden lamps' create mainly visual imagery or sound imagery?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Padho: 'Paani se bhari sadak par kagaz ki naavein streetlights ke neeche tiny golden lamps jaisi beh rahi thi.' 'Tiny golden lamps' se mainly visual imagery banti hai ya sound imagery?
hints: Which sense helps you imagine the comparison?
Think about what streetlights reveal in the scene.
The comparison helps you picture the boats’ ___.
Visual imagery: the comparison helps you picture their appearance.

ongrade.prompt_en: Complete both verbs in the simple present: 'The bundle of paper boats ___ (float) downstream, while the children ___ (watch) from the bridge.'
ongrade.prompt_hi: Simple present mein dono verbs bharo: 'The bundle of paper boats ___ (float) downstream, while the children ___ (watch) from the bridge.'
hints: What is the main noun in each subject?
Match each verb with its subject, not the nearest noun.
The bundle ___ downstream; the children ___ from the bridge.
Floats; watch: 'bundle' is singular, while 'children' is plural.

openers.prompt_en: Read this note to a friend: 'The night train to Jaipur was delayed, but I loved watching the sunrise over the fields. I wish you were here!' Is the writer's tone mainly excited or angry?
openers.prompt_hi: Friend ko likha note padho: 'Jaipur ki night train late thi, lekin kheton par sunrise dekhkar maza aa gaya. Kaash tum yahan hote!' Writer ka tone mainly excited hai ya angry?
hints: Which feeling lasts beyond the train delay?
Notice how the writer describes the sunrise.
The writer's main feeling is ____.
Excited: the writer enjoyed the sunrise despite the delay.

openers.prompt_en: Meera is writing an informal letter from Kochi to her cousin. Which should appear immediately before 'Dear Riya': 'Kochi, 8 August' or 'Your cousin, Meera'?
openers.prompt_hi: Meera Kochi se apni cousin ko informal letter likh rahi hai. 'Dear Riya' se turant pehle kya aayega: 'Kochi, 8 August' ya 'Your cousin, Meera'?
hints: Where does the greeting go in a letter?
Think about what belongs at the top, not the end.
Immediately before the greeting comes the ____.
Kochi, 8 August: place and date come before the greeting.

harder.prompt_en: A travel letter has these parts: 'Dear Kabir', 'With love', 'Pune, 3 October', 'I reached Mysuru today', 'Sana'. Which part must move to the beginning to correct the letter's order?
harder.prompt_hi: Travel letter ke parts hain: 'Dear Kabir', 'With love', 'Pune, 3 October', 'I reached Mysuru today', 'Sana'. Letter ka order theek karne ke liye kaunsa part shuru mein lana hoga?
hints: What usually appears above the greeting?
Check which part tells where and when it was written.
Move ____ to the beginning.
Pune, 3 October: the place and date begin an informal letter.

harder.prompt_en: Complete the travel update with three prepositions in order: 'We boarded the train ___ Surat ___ Friday and arrived ___ Goa before sunset.'
harder.prompt_hi: Travel update mein teen prepositions order mein bharo: 'We boarded the train ___ Surat ___ Friday and arrived ___ Goa before sunset.'
acceptable: at Surat, on Friday, in Goa
hints: Do places and days take the same preposition?
Distinguish a boarding point, a day, and a state.
We boarded ___ Surat ___ Friday and arrived ___ Goa.
At, on, in: use them for a boarding point, day, and state.

harder.prompt_en: Your friend in Delhi writes, 'Which direction is Kerala from here? Tell me one thing about it.' Which reply answers both requests: A) 'Kerala is south of Delhi and is known for its backwaters.' B) 'Kerala is beautiful. Visit soon.'?
harder.prompt_hi: Delhi mein tumhara friend likhta hai, 'Yahan se Kerala kis direction mein hai? Uske baare mein ek baat batao.' Kaunsa reply dono sawaalon ka jawab deta hai: A) 'Kerala is south of Delhi and is known for its backwaters.' B) 'Kerala is beautiful. Visit soon.'?
hints: How many things did your friend ask?
A complete reply needs a direction and a place detail.
Choose the reply that includes ____ and ____.
A: it gives both Kerala's direction and a detail about it.

ongrade.prompt_en: Read this letter extract: 'Dear Rohan, I wish you could have seen the sunrise over the hills in Sikkim! The climb was tiring, but the view made it worthwhile.' Is the writer’s tone mainly enthusiastic or regretful?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Yeh letter extract padho: 'Dear Rohan, I wish you could have seen the sunrise over the hills in Sikkim! The climb was tiring, but the view made it worthwhile.' Writer ka tone mainly enthusiastic hai ya regretful?
hints: Which feeling stands out after the climb?
Notice how the writer describes the view.
The view made the tiring climb ___ for the writer.
Enthusiastic: the writer celebrates the view despite the tiring climb.

ongrade.prompt_en: In a letter to your cousin, you have written: 'Dear Farah, I reached Srinagar yesterday.' You still need to add 'Lucknow, 8 June'. Should it go before 'Dear Farah' or after the closing?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Cousin ko letter mein tumne likha: 'Dear Farah, I reached Srinagar yesterday.' Ab 'Lucknow, 8 June' add karna hai. Yeh 'Dear Farah' se pehle aayega ya closing ke baad?
hints: Which part tells the reader where and when you wrote?
An informal letter places that detail above the greeting.
'Lucknow, 8 June' goes ___ the greeting.
Before 'Dear Farah': place and date come above the greeting.

ongrade.prompt_en: Complete both blanks with the correct preposition: 'Our train stopped ___ Agra for ten minutes. We spent the night ___ the train.' Give the two words in order.
ongrade.prompt_hi: Dono blanks mein sahi preposition lagao: 'Our train stopped ___ Agra for ten minutes. We spent the night ___ the train.' Dono words order mein batao.
hints: Does each blank describe a stop or being aboard?
Use different prepositions for a stopping point and train travel.
Our train stopped ___ Agra; we slept ___ the train.
At, on: the train stopped at Agra; we slept on the train.

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'During the school play, Meera reached for the curtain rope. It jerked upward before she touched it.' What is more likely: someone is pulling the rope from backstage, or the play has ended?
openers.prompt_hi: Padho: 'School play mein Meera curtain ki rassi pakadne wali thi. Chhoone se pehle hi woh upar khinch gayi.' Kya zyada likely hai: backstage se koi rassi kheench raha hai, ya play khatam ho gaya?
openers.answer: Someone is pulling the rope from backstage
acceptable: Backstage se koi rassi kheench raha hai
hints: What happened before Meera touched the rope?
Use the unexpected movement as your clue.
The rope may be moving because ___.
Someone is pulling it backstage; it moved before Meera touched it.

verified.solverAnswer: someone is pulling the rope from backstage

openers.prompt_en: At a cricket match, the writer says, 'Crack! The bat met the ball.' Which word imitates a sound: 'crack' or 'met'?
openers.prompt_hi: Cricket match ke baare mein writer kehta hai, 'Crack! Bat ball se takraya.' Kaunsa word awaaz ki nakal karta hai: 'crack' ya 'met'?
hints: Which word can you almost hear?
A sound word imitates a noise, rather than naming an action.
The sound-imitating word is ___.
‘Crack’ imitates the sharp sound of bat meeting ball.

harder.prompt_en: Compare: 'The metro arrived' and 'With a metallic screech, the metro slid beside the crowded platform.' What does 'metallic screech' add: a sound you can imagine, or the metro's arrival time?
harder.prompt_hi: Compare karo: 'The metro arrived' aur 'With a metallic screech, the metro slid beside the crowded platform.' 'Metallic screech' kya add karta hai: imagine karne layak awaaz, ya metro ka arrival time?
hints: Which sense does the phrase appeal to?
Think about what the extra words help readers experience.
They help readers imagine a ___.
A sound you can imagine; ‘screech’ describes what readers might hear.

harder.prompt_en: Fill all three blanks in order: 'At the science fair, I met ___ university student. She showed me ___ unusual robot. ___ robot could sort waste.'
harder.prompt_hi: Teenon blanks order mein bharo: 'At the science fair, I met ___ university student. She showed me ___ unusual robot. ___ robot could sort waste.'
hints: Is each noun new to the listener or already mentioned?
For new nouns, listen to the opening sound; for repeated nouns, use the definite article.
The articles, in order, are ___, ___, ___.
A, an, the: ‘university’ begins with a consonant sound; ‘robot’ is then repeated.

harder.prompt_en: Read: 'A forest guard stopped hikers from leaving food beside a hillside trail. A leopard had been seen nearby, and she wanted it to keep hunting in the forest.' Why did she stop them?
harder.prompt_hi: Padho: 'Forest guard ne hikers ko pahaadi trail ke paas khana chhodne se roka. Wahan leopard dekha gaya tha, aur woh chahti thi ki woh jungle mein hi shikar kare.' Usne hikers ko kyun roka?
harder.answer: To avoid attracting the leopard to people with food
acceptable: So the leopard would not come near people for food
Leopard ko khane ke liye logon ke paas aane se rokne ke liye
To keep the leopard hunting in the forest
hints: What might leftover food encourage the leopard to do?
Connect the hikers’ food with the guard’s wish about hunting.
She wanted to prevent the leopard from ___.
She wanted to avoid attracting the leopard to people with food.

verified.solverAnswer: To prevent the leopard from becoming dependent on human food and to keep it hunting in the forest.

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'My suitcase waits beneath my bed; / I trace new roads across a map. / The school bell calls me back each day.' Which best describes the speaker: eager to travel, tired of schoolwork, or afraid of roads?
openers.prompt_hi: Ye lines padho: 'My suitcase waits beneath my bed; / I trace new roads across a map. / The school bell calls me back each day.' Speaker ko sabse achchha kya describe karta hai: eager to travel, tired of schoolwork, ya afraid of roads?
hints: What does the speaker keep thinking about?
Notice the suitcase and the roads on the map.
Together, these details show the speaker is ___ .
Eager to travel: the speaker imagines journeys while still at school.

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'Across the quiet harbour, a ship's horn sounds after sunset.' Which detail is sound imagery: the quiet harbour, the ship's horn, or the sunset?
openers.prompt_hi: Padho: 'Across the quiet harbour, a ship's horn sounds after sunset.' Sound imagery kaunsi detail hai: the quiet harbour, the ship's horn, ya the sunset?
acceptable: the sound of the ship's horn
hints: Which detail could you hear?
Sound imagery helps you imagine a noise.
The noise in this sentence comes from ___ .
The ship's horn: it is the sound described in the sentence.

harder.prompt_en: Read: 'At midnight, a distant ferry horn crosses the still water. Meera stands at her window, imagining the shore beyond.' Why does the distant horn strengthen the mood of longing? Answer in a short phrase.
harder.prompt_hi: Padho: 'At midnight, a distant ferry horn crosses the still water. Meera stands at her window, imagining the shore beyond.' Door ki horn longing ka mood kyun badhati hai? Short phrase mein batao.
harder.answer: It suggests a journey Meera can hear but cannot yet take.
acceptable: The sound reminds her of a journey she cannot yet take.
It makes a faraway journey feel close but out of reach.
hints: Where is Meera while the ferry moves?
Compare the sound reaching her with the journey itself.
She can hear the ferry, but she cannot ___ .
It suggests a journey she hears but cannot yet take.

verified.solverAnswer: A faraway sound symbolizes unreachable destinations.

harder.prompt_en: Ayaan is in Pune today, but he wants to be in Jaipur for the kite festival. Complete his present wish: 'I wish I ___ in Jaipur today.'
harder.prompt_hi: Ayaan aaj Pune mein hai, par kite festival ke liye Jaipur mein hona chahta hai. Uski present wish complete karo: 'I wish I ___ in Jaipur today.'
hints: Is Ayaan describing where he is or where he wishes to be?
For an unreal present wish, use a special past-form verb.
After 'I wish I', the verb for location is ___ .
Were: 'I wish I were in Jaipur' expresses an unreal present wish.

harder.prompt_en: Join these feelings in one sentence beginning with 'Although': 'Nisha enjoys the school trip to Mysuru. She misses her family.'
harder.prompt_hi: In dono feelings ko 'Although' se shuru hone wale ek sentence mein jodo: 'Nisha enjoys the school trip to Mysuru. She misses her family.'
harder.answer: Although Nisha enjoys the school trip to Mysuru, she misses her family.
acceptable: Although Nisha misses her family, she enjoys the school trip to Mysuru.
hints: Which two feelings seem to pull in different directions?
Put one feeling after 'Although' and the other after a comma.
Although Nisha ___, she ___ .
Although Nisha enjoys the trip, she misses her family; both feelings coexist.

verified.solverAnswer: Although Nisha enjoys the school trip to Mysuru, she misses her family.

openers.prompt_en: For a school newsletter, put Meera’s events in time order: (A) She won a district race in July. (B) She began training in January. (C) She entered her first race in March.
openers.prompt_hi: School newsletter ke liye Meera ke events time order mein lagao: (A) July mein district race jeeti. (B) January mein training shuru ki. (C) March mein apni pehli race mein bhaag liya.
hints: Which month comes earliest?
Follow the dates, not the order of the sentences.
Start with ___; then check March and July.
B, C, A: January comes before March and July.

openers.prompt_en: After an injury, Kabir could not join the kabaddi team. He attended every practice and trained for next season. Which value does this best show: determination or honesty?
openers.prompt_hi: Injury ke baad Kabir kabaddi team mein nahi khel saka. Woh har practice mein gaya aur agle season ke liye training karta raha. Yeh kaunsi value dikhata hai: determination ya honesty?
hints: What did Kabir keep doing after the setback?
Choose the value shown by continuing to work towards a goal.
Continuing to train shows ___.
Determination: he kept training despite missing the team.

harder.prompt_en: After an accident, Sana practised walking with a prosthetic leg. She entered a school trek even though she was nervous. Why does entering the trek show courage rather than a lack of fear? Answer in a short phrase.
harder.prompt_hi: Accident ke baad Sana ne prosthetic leg ke saath chalne ki practice ki. Ghabrahat ke bawajood usne school trek mein naam likhaya. Yeh fear na hone ke bajay courage kyun dikhata hai? Chhote phrase mein batao.
acceptable: she went ahead although she was nervous
dar ke bawajood usne koshish ki
hints: Was Sana completely free of worry?
Courage concerns what someone does while facing fear.
She felt nervous, but she still ___.
She acted despite fear: nervousness did not stop her.

verified.solverAnswer: Courage is acting despite fear, not without it.

harder.prompt_en: Complete this life-story sentence using the simple past of both verbs: “Ravi ___ (fall) during a cycling race but ___ (fight) to finish it.”
harder.prompt_hi: Life-story sentence ko dono verbs ke simple past se complete karo: “Ravi ___ (fall) during a cycling race but ___ (fight) to finish it.”
acceptable: Ravi fell during a cycling race but fought to finish it
hints: Did the race happen now or earlier?
Both verbs have irregular simple-past forms.
Ravi ___ during the race but ___ to finish.
Fell; fought: both tell what Ravi did in the past.

harder.prompt_en: For a report about a difficult trek, choose the correct pair of opposites: “The route seemed ___ at first, and the guides ___ about the safest path.” Options: “impossible, disagreed” or “unpossible, unagreed”.
harder.prompt_hi: Difficult trek ki report ke liye opposites ki sahi jodi chuno: “The route seemed ___ at first, and the guides ___ about the safest path.” Options: “impossible, disagreed” ya “unpossible, unagreed”.
hints: Which pair uses standard English prefixes?
Different base words can take different negative prefixes.
The route seemed ___, and the guides ___.
Impossible, disagreed: these are the standard opposites of possible and agreed.

ongrade.prompt_en: A biography says: “In 2016, Nisha began training for a high-altitude trek. Two years later, she completed her first mountain climb. In 2021, she guided a school trekking team.” How many years after beginning training did she become a guide?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Biography mein hai: “2016 mein Nisha ne high-altitude trek ki training shuru ki. Do saal baad usne pehli mountain climb poori ki. 2021 mein usne school trekking team ko guide kiya.” Training shuru karne ke kitne saal baad woh guide bani?
hints: Which two events does the question connect?
Use the dates for training and guiding, not the first climb.
Years between those events = ___ − ___.
5 years; subtract 2016 from 2021.

ongrade.prompt_en: After an injury, Aditi’s first trek ended early. She changed her training plan, practised for months and attempted the trek again. Which value is best supported: determination, generosity or honesty?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Injury ke baad Aditi ka pehla trek jaldi khatam ho gaya. Usne training plan badla, mahino practice ki aur dobara trek try kiya. Kaunsi value sabse achchhi tarah dikhti hai: determination, generosity ya honesty?
hints: What did Aditi do after the first attempt?
Look for the value shown by continuing towards a goal.
Changing plans and trying again show ___.
Determination; she kept working towards the trek despite a setback.

ongrade.prompt_en: Complete the biography sentence with the simple past of the verbs in brackets: “When the trail became slippery, the climber ___ (fall), but her teammates ___ (fight) through the storm to bring help.”
ongrade.prompt_hi: Biography sentence ko brackets wale verbs ke simple past se complete karo: “When the trail became slippery, the climber ___ (fall), but her teammates ___ (fight) through the storm to bring help.”
hints: Are these events happening now or already over?
Both verbs have irregular simple-past forms.
The climber ___; her teammates ___.
Fell; fought. Both are irregular simple-past forms.

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'Aarav: Why is our school collecting letters? Teacher: We will send them to soldiers posted far from home. Aarav: I’ll write one tonight.' What does Aarav plan to do, and who will receive it?
openers.prompt_hi: Padho: 'Aarav: Why is our school collecting letters? Teacher: We will send them to soldiers posted far from home. Aarav: I’ll write one tonight.' Aarav kya karne wala hai, aur letter kise milega?
openers.answer: Aarav plans to write a letter for soldiers posted far from home.
acceptable: He will write a letter to soldiers posted far from home.
Write a letter for soldiers away from home
hints: What will Aarav do tonight?
Connect his final line with the teacher’s explanation.
Aarav will write ___ for ___.
He will write a letter for soldiers posted far from home.

verified.solverAnswer: Aarav plans to write a letter, and it will be received by soldiers posted far from home.

openers.prompt_en: At a school assembly, Meera said, 'I respect the rescue team.' Which report is correct: 'Meera said that she respected the rescue team' or 'Meera said that I respect the rescue team'?
openers.prompt_hi: School assembly mein Meera ne kaha, 'I respect the rescue team.' Kaunsi report sahi hai: 'Meera said that she respected the rescue team' ya 'Meera said that I respect the rescue team'?
openers.answer: Meera said that she respected the rescue team.
acceptable: Meera said that she respected the rescue team
hints: Who does ‘I’ refer to in Meera’s words?
In a report, adjust the speaker’s pronoun and present-tense verb.
Meera said that ___ ___ the rescue team.
Meera said that she respected the rescue team; both pronoun and tense change.

verified.solverAnswer: Meera said that she respected the rescue team.

harder.prompt_en: A reporter asked Captain Rao, 'Why did you return to the flooded village?' Report the reporter’s question in indirect speech.
harder.prompt_hi: Ek reporter ne Captain Rao se poochha, 'Why did you return to the flooded village?' Reporter ka sawaal indirect speech mein batao.
harder.answer: The reporter asked Captain Rao why he had returned to the flooded village.
acceptable: The reporter asked Captain Rao why he had returned to the flooded village
The reporter asked why Captain Rao had returned to the flooded village
hints: Is the reporter asking for a reason?
Keep the question word; change the pronoun and verb tense.
The reporter asked Captain Rao why ___ ___ returned to the flooded village.
The reporter asked why he had returned; indirect questions use statement word order.

verified.solverAnswer: The reporter asked Captain Rao why he had returned to the flooded village.

harder.prompt_en: A plaque names the firefighters who died while saving families. Students leave flowers there each year. Which word best names this place: memorial, comrade, or valour?
harder.prompt_hi: Ek plaque par un firefighters ke naam hain jo families ko bachate hue shaheed hue. Students har saal wahaan phool rakhte hain. Is jagah ke liye kaunsa word sahi hai: memorial, comrade, ya valour?
hints: Are you naming a place, a person, or a quality?
Choose the word for a place that honours people who died.
This place is a ___.
Memorial; it is a place where people remember and honour them.

harder.prompt_en: You are interviewing a veteran for the school magazine. Which question is more respectful: 'Did you ever feel scared, or is that embarrassing?' or 'Would you be comfortable sharing how you handled difficult moments?' Why?
harder.prompt_hi: School magazine ke liye tum ek veteran ka interview le rahe ho. Kaunsa sawaal zyada respectful hai: 'Did you ever feel scared, or is that embarrassing?' ya 'Would you be comfortable sharing how you handled difficult moments?' Kyun?
harder.answer: The second question; it lets the veteran choose what to share without suggesting that fear is embarrassing.
acceptable: The second; it gives the veteran a choice and avoids judging their feelings.
The second question because it is considerate and does not pressure the veteran.
hints: Which question gives the veteran more control over their answer?
Consider whether either question judges the veteran’s feelings.
The ___ question is respectful because it ___.
The second; it invites sharing without pressure or judgement.

verified.solverAnswer: Would you be comfortable sharing how you handled difficult moments?

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'At the school gate, our flags rise high; / Far away, you watch the border sky.' Is the speaker mainly praising the flags or thanking the soldiers? Why?
openers.prompt_hi: Ye lines padho: 'At the school gate, our flags rise high; / Far away, you watch the border sky.' Speaker flags ki tareef kar raha hai ya soldiers ka shukriya ada kar raha hai? Kyun?
openers.answer: Thanking the soldiers for guarding the border
acceptable: soldiers, because they watch the border
soldiers ko border ki rakhwali ke liye thanks
hints: Who does the word 'you' address?
Notice what that person does while the school celebrates.
The speaker thanks ___ for watching the border.
The soldiers: their border duty makes the celebration possible.

verified.solverAnswer: Thanking the soldiers, because the second line acknowledges their far-away duty.

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'The stadium roars beneath bright lights; / A soldier keeps watch through silent nights.' Which contrast stands out: noise and silence, or summer and winter?
openers.prompt_hi: Ye lines padho: 'The stadium roars beneath bright lights; / A soldier keeps watch through silent nights.' Kaunsa contrast dikhta hai: noise aur silence, ya summer aur winter?
acceptable: the roaring stadium and silent nights
hints: Which words describe the stadium and the night?
Compare what can be heard in each scene.
The contrast is between ___ and ___.
Noise and silence: the stadium roars, but the night is silent.

harder.prompt_en: Read: 'Steam rises from our Diwali dinner; / Frost settles on a guard's gloves.' Why does the writer place these two images together?
harder.prompt_hi: Ye lines padho: 'Steam rises from our Diwali dinner; / Frost settles on a guard's gloves.' Writer ne ye do images saath kyun rakhi hain?
harder.answer: To contrast our comfort with the guard's hardship
acceptable: to show our comfort and the guard's hardship
to contrast warmth at home with cold on duty
ghar ki garmahat aur guard ki mushkil dikhane ke liye
hints: How does each scene feel?
Think about warmth at home and conditions on duty.
The images contrast our ___ with the guard's ___.
Our comfort contrasts with the guard's hardship, inviting gratitude.

verified.solverAnswer: To contrast civilian comfort with a soldier's harsh duty.

harder.prompt_en: A report mentions several soldiers and the letters they wrote home. Complete: 'The ___ letters reached their families.' Choose: soldiers, soldier's, or soldiers'.
harder.prompt_hi: Report mein kai soldiers aur unke ghar bheje letters ka zikr hai. Complete karo: 'The ___ letters reached their families.' Chuno: soldiers, soldier's, ya soldiers'.
hints: Are the letters linked to one person or several?
Use the possessive form for a plural noun ending in s.
For several soldiers, write soldiers__ before 'letters'.
Soldiers': the apostrophe shows the letters belong to several soldiers.

harder.prompt_en: At a school event, you want to thank soldiers for keeping mountain roads safe. Complete the message with the correct form of 'protect': 'Thank you for ___ travellers on these roads.'
harder.prompt_hi: School event mein tum soldiers ko mountain roads safe rakhne ke liye thank karna chahte ho. 'Protect' ka sahi form lagao: 'Thank you for ___ travellers on these roads.'
acceptable: thank you for protecting travellers on these roads
hints: What verb form follows 'Thank you for'?
The action needs an -ing ending here.
Thank you for ___ travellers on these roads.
Protecting: 'Thank you for' takes an -ing verb.

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'Savitribai Phule trained as a teacher. She then opened a school for girls in Pune and later helped open more schools.' What did she achieve after becoming a teacher?
openers.prompt_hi: Padho: 'Savitribai Phule trained as a teacher. She then opened a school for girls in Pune and later helped open more schools.' Teacher banne ke baad unhone kya kiya?
openers.answer: She opened a school for girls in Pune.
acceptable: Opened a girls’ school in Pune
She opened a school for girls
hints: Which event comes just after her training?
Follow the order signalled by 'then' and 'later'.
After training, she ___ in Pune.
She opened a girls’ school in Pune; 'then' places it next.

verified.solverAnswer: She opened a school for girls in Pune and helped open more schools.

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'During a flood, village leader Amina asked families to share their boats so everyone could reach safety.' Which value does her decision best show: unity or pride?
openers.prompt_hi: Padho: 'During a flood, village leader Amina asked families to share their boats so everyone could reach safety.' Unke faisle se kaunsi value dikhti hai: unity ya pride?
hints: Did she ask families to act separately or together?
Choose the value supported by sharing resources for everyone.
Sharing boats for everyone's safety shows ___.
Unity: the families worked together to help everyone.

harder.prompt_en: Read: 'When an invading army approached, Commander Leela let neighbouring villages help plan the defence instead of giving orders alone.' Why does this show leadership rather than just courage?
harder.prompt_hi: Padho: 'When an invading army approached, Commander Leela let neighbouring villages help plan the defence instead of giving orders alone.' Yeh sirf courage nahi, leadership kaise dikhata hai?
harder.answer: She brought people together to plan the defence.
acceptable: She united the villages to plan
She listened to others and planned with them
hints: Who took part in making the plan?
Leadership can mean making space for others' ideas.
She showed leadership by ___ in planning.
She brought people together to plan; she did not act alone.

verified.solverAnswer: She involved others in decision-making, showing guidance and collaboration, not just bravery.

harder.prompt_en: Join these facts in one sentence using 'which': 'The coastal watchtower warned Ullal of approaching ships. The watchtower stood near the harbour.' Begin: 'The coastal watchtower...'
harder.prompt_hi: 'Which' use karke ek sentence banao: 'The coastal watchtower warned Ullal of approaching ships. The watchtower stood near the harbour.' 'The coastal watchtower...' se shuru karo.
harder.answer: The coastal watchtower, which stood near the harbour, warned Ullal of approaching ships.
acceptable: The coastal watchtower which stood near the harbour warned Ullal of approaching ships.
hints: Which detail tells us more about the watchtower?
Place the extra detail beside the noun it describes.
The coastal watchtower, which ___, warned Ullal of approaching ships.
The watchtower, which stood near the harbour, warned Ullal; 'which' adds detail.

verified.solverAnswer: The coastal watchtower, which stood near the harbour, warned Ullal of approaching ships.

harder.prompt_en: Change to the passive, keeping the time phrase: 'In 1525, the defenders repaired the harbour wall.'
harder.prompt_hi: Time phrase ko rakhe hue passive voice mein badlo: 'In 1525, the defenders repaired the harbour wall.'
harder.answer: In 1525, the harbour wall was repaired by the defenders.
acceptable: The harbour wall was repaired by the defenders in 1525.
In 1525, the harbour wall was repaired.
hints: What received the action?
Put that noun first, then use the past passive form.
In 1525, the harbour wall ___ by the defenders.
The harbour wall was repaired by the defenders; it received the action.

verified.solverAnswer: In 1525, the harbour wall was repaired by the defenders.
